issues.description: The problem statement's UML and the solution expect a Stock.emptyStock() method, but the template Stock class provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This name/signature mismatch is structural: students following the problem/spec will look for or implement emptyStock(), but the template does not declare it (and tests/solution use emptyStock). This can confuse students and cause compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the specification and solution by renaming clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a public emptyStock() method that delegates to clearInventory(). Update any references accordingly so that the method name is consistent across problem statement, template, and solution.

issues.description: The Stock class method that clears the inventory is named differently in the template repository versus the problem statement and solution. The problem statement and solution expect emptyStock(), but the template Stock class provides clearInventory(). This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual operation (emptying the stock) can confuse students mapping the requirement to the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (or add an emptyStock() wrapper that calls clearInventory()) so the starter code matches the problem statement and the solution naming.
